title: The Longest Day
note: b385. No pose rig supports true upside-down (the rig has no 'lying on back' knob, only tilt/lift around the feet), so p8's 'Ned asleep upside down with his feet in the air' reuses the existing 'sprawl' pose (a comic flat tumble) with a sleepy eye rather than risking an invented 180-degree pose that could render badly — the gag still reads as 'collapsed asleep in an undignified heap'. P1's 'long shadows the wrong way round' and p7's hard light/shadow contrast are not literally drawable (the kit has no directional-shadow mechanism) and are simplified to bright/sleepy compositions instead.

pages.brief: Very early summer morning. The sun already high over the garden while Pip is still asleep in the ivy nest, one eye squinting open in disbelief. Long shadows the wrong way round. Pale washed-out gold.
pages.alt: Very early summer morning, the sun already high over the garden, while Pip squints one eye open in disbelief from the ivy nest.

pages.brief: Ned the gold duckling standing on the pond edge in a running pose, chest out, utterly convinced of himself. A frog and a fish in the water beside him looking distinctly unimpressed.
pages.alt: Ned the duckling stands on the pond edge in a running pose, chest out and utterly convinced of himself, while a frog and a fish in the water look distinctly unimpressed.

pages.brief: Pip perched on a stone with both wings clamped over where his ears would be. Ned mid-quack, beak wide, drawn slightly bigger than life. Comic size contrast.
pages.alt: Pip perches on a stone with both wings clamped over his ears, while Ned, drawn slightly bigger than life, quacks with his beak wide open — a comic size contrast.

pages.brief: Moss the hedgehog ambling along a garden path with a leaf on his back, taking his time. Pip and Ned already tiny in the distance ahead. Warm and completely unhurried.
pages.alt: Moss the hedgehog ambles along a garden path with a leaf on his back, taking his time, while Pip and Ned are already tiny in the distance ahead.

pages.brief: Looking straight up the old oak. Pip a small speck near the very top, wings out. The trunk enormous below him. Vertical composition to sell the height — deliberately tiny and distant; that smallness IS the joke of the page.
pages.alt: Looking straight up the huge trunk of the old oak, with Pip just a small speck near the very top, wings spread.

pages.brief: Three-step sequence across the page: Ned scrambling onto a low branch, Ned slipping to a lower one, Ned sitting in the grass with a leaf on his head. Same pose, three stages. Very funny.
pages.alt: A three-step sequence: Ned scrambling onto a low branch, then slipping to a lower one, then sitting in the grass with a leaf on his head — the same pose, three funny stages.

pages.brief: All three squashed together in a strip of deep cool shadow under the hedge, panting slightly. The rest of the page bleached bright with heat. Strong light-dark contrast.
pages.alt: All three friends squeeze together into a strip of deep cool shade under the hedge, panting slightly, with the rest of the page bleached bright by the heat.

pages.brief: Moss curled into a ball, fast asleep; Pip asleep on top of him; Ned asleep upside down with his feet in the air. Late evening light, still not dark. Peaceful and silly.
pages.alt: Moss is curled into a ball fast asleep with Pip asleep on top of him, and Ned collapsed asleep in a silly heap beside them, in the late evening light.
